{{Short description|Mathematician, writer and translator}}
'''Baruch ben Jehuda Löb Lindau''' ({{Langx|he| בָּרוּךְ{{popdf}} בֶּן יְהוּדָה לֵייבּ לינדא}}; 1759, [[Hanover]], [[Holy Roman Empire]] – 5 December 1849, [[Berlin]], [[Kingdom of Prussia|Prussia]]) was a [[History of the Jews in Germany|Jewish-German]] [[mathematician]], [[science writer]], and translator.

Lindau became a member of the [[Haskalah|maskilim]] circle in Berlin, publishing articles on science and scientific instruments in ''[[Me'assefim|ha-Me'assef]]''. He was a counselor of the maskilic association ''Chevrat shocharai Ha'tov ve'hatushiya'' and translated several ''[[Haftarah|haftarot]]'' into German for [[Moses Mendelssohn|Mendelssohn]]'s ''[[Biurists|Bi'ur]]'' project.{{r|aleph|page=287}}

In 1789, he published ''{{ill|Reshit Limmudim|he|ראשית לימודים}}'', his most successful work. It was a Hebrew scientific textbook containing sections on astronomy, physics, biology, and geography. The second part, ''Reshit Limmudim'', was published in 1810 and devoted to physics, chemistry, and mechanics.{{r|aleph|page=286}} The work remained a popular scientific encyclopedia among European Jews for nearly a century.<ref>{{cite book|title=המשכילים במדעים: חינוך יהודי למדעים במרחב דובר הגרמנית בעת החדשה|first=Tal|last=Kogman|year=2013|language=Hebrew|publisher=Magnes Press|pages=54–56|isbn=978-965-493-723-8|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XIqsjgEACAAJ}}</ref>
